🐛 Fix `on_startup` and `on_shutdown` parameters of `APIRouter`

This fixes the issue reported in this comment: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14851#issuecomment-3863896385

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI


def s_start():
    print("SYNC START", flush=True)


app = FastAPI(on_startup=[s_start])
```

And `_shutdown` is probably similar.

The issue is that `APIRouter.__init__` does:
```python
        self.on_startup: list[Callable[[], Any]] = (
            [] if on_startup is None else list(on_startup)
        )
        self.on_shutdown: list[Callable[[], Any]] = (
            [] if on_shutdown is None else list(on_shutdown)
        )
        # ...
        super().__init__(
            routes=routes,
            redirect_slashes=redirect_slashes,
            default=default,
            lifespan=lifespan_context,
        )
```

If `super().__init__` (Starlette's `Router.__init__`) sets `self.on_startup = []` and `self.on_shutdown = []`, then the values passed to `APIRouter` are lost.

Wait, if Starlette removed support for `on_startup` and `on_shutdown`, why would it set them to `[]`?

The issue says:
"Startup event is not called because `APIRouter.on_startup` is set in `APIRouter.__init__` before calling `super().__init__` and is overridden by `router.__init__` (https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/blob/e5b8a5d200504a2608bed11fe6f66b1d20b9ae2c/starlette/routing.py#L597-L598)"

If I look at the link (even though I can't access it, I can trust the issue description), it seems `starlette.routing.Router.__init__` does something that overrides `on_startup` and `on_shutdown`.

So the fix is to move the assignment of `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` after `super().__init__`.

But wait, `lifespan_context` is created before `super().__init__`.
```python
        # Determine the lifespan context to use
        if lifespan is None:
            # Use the default lifespan that runs on_startup/on_shutdown handlers
            lifespan_context: Lifespan[Any] = _DefaultLifespan(self)
        # ...
        super().__init__(
            routes=routes,
            redirect_slashes=redirect_slashes,
            default=default,
            lifespan=lifespan_context,
        )
```
`_DefaultLifespan(self)` just stores `self`. When it's eventually called (during app startup), it calls `self._startup()`, which iterates over `self.on_startup`.

So if we move the assignment of `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` after `super().__init__`, it should work, because `_DefaultLifespan` will access the values of `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` at the time of startup, not at the time of `_DefaultLifespan` creation.
